analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (2 November 2026)
key_insights: US equities fell Friday: S&P 500 -1.82%, Nasdaq -2.86% (worst session since June), Dow -1.09%. The AI trade was the biggest drag, with semis, memory and neoclouds sharply lower. NVDA and SPCX fared worst among big tech. Equal-weight RSP outpaced the cap-weighted index by about 100 bp.

Treasuries rallied on flight-to-safety buying, with yields down 2-8 bp. Gold fell 3.3% (the table shows -3.65%), its worst day since June, and closed back below $4K. Bitcoin futures lost 5.2% after the Binance hack. WTI crude gained 2.1% on skepticism about a diplomatic offramp in Iran.

Amazon fell after earnings. AWS growth of 39% beat expectations but fell short of elevated buyside expectations. Q3 capex of $77B was about $20B above consensus, TTM FCF was -$42B, and management plans to spend 'meaningfully more' in 2027. Retail and advertising slowed and missed, and Q4 operating income guidance was below consensus at the midpoint. AWS backlog rose to $578B.

Intel fell 28.6%. Q3 EPS beat but revenue missed. Client Computing revenue fell 5.1% y/y to $8.1B against a $8.95B consensus. Q4 EPS and revenue guidance came in well below the Street. The company expects the PC market to fall 10% in 2027 after a 12% decline this year, citing memory shortages and high component costs. Capex is $20B this year with a significant increase in 2027 and negative FCF. An Israeli factory shutdown cuts revenue by $600M over two quarters. BofA downgraded the stock to neutral from buy.

The megacap tech and semis selloff raises scrutiny of AI funding ahead of Anthropic's expected November IPO. Alphabet is 22% below its $85B June equity offering price, Intel is 33% below its $23B August offer, and Meta's $25B offering is already more than 2% underwater. Blackstone said Anthropic's $63B chip financing is expected to get a high junk rating after the IPO. Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual contracts on Hyperliquid are down about 25% from the 9-Sep peak.

Binance confirmed $6.3B of funds were impacted in a suspected hack, described as the biggest crypto heist ever. Binance froze $3B and suspended deposits and withdrawals temporarily, and said it will cover losses. TRM Labs attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit. Tether and Circle froze $2.54B in linked assets. Coinbase said it was unaffected.

Renewed US strikes on Iran remain on the table after the midterm elections next Tuesday. Iran's Ghalibaf insists the US must first meet preconditions (end the blockade, unfreeze assets, restart oil sales) before nuclear talks resume. CENTCOM commander Cooper gave Trump an in-person briefing. Qatari negotiators are continuing talks in Tehran.

Post-FOMC Fedspeak stayed firm: Dallas Fed's Logan said two more 25 bp hikes are needed before pausing, and St. Louis Fed's Musalem said another hike may come soon. Rate path pricing was modestly dovish after a less-hawkish policy assessment. October payrolls are due next Friday, with consensus at +40K.
US data was light. Q3 ECI rose 0.8% m/m, in line. October Chicago PMI was 55.3 against 56.0 consensus, with prices paid at their highest since December 2021.

The ECB held rates but a December hike is likely unless growth deteriorates notably, with a pause expected after that. Lagarde said a hike was discussed and stressed upside inflation risk. ECB staff estimate the rise in bond yields cuts growth by a cumulative 100 bps and inflation by 90 bps over 2027-28 against the September baseline. Lagarde will step down on 7-Feb, with de Cos and Knot the leading candidates.

Eurozone October national inflation diverged. German CPI fell to 2.8% y/y from 3.3% (core 2.1% from 2.4%) on a temporary fuel tax cut. France rose to 3.4% from 3.1%. Italy jumped to 5.4% from 4.2% against a 4.6% consensus. Spain held at 4.9%. Pantheon raised its Eurozone October inflation forecast to 4% ahead of the 4-Nov flash HICP.

The UK Budget was low-key. The OBR cut 2027 growth to 1.0% from 1.6%, and the gilt reaction was muted. Markets price over a 90% chance of a 25 bp BoE hike next week to 4% and about a 50% chance of a December move, with a 6-3 vote split tipped. BoE DMP year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 3.3% from 3.1%.

STOXX 600 Q3 earnings growth is 35.8% y/y among the 43% that have reported (blended 26.3%), against 18.9% expected at the start of the season. Sales are up 11.3%, with an aggregate earnings surprise of +2.85% and a sales surprise of -2.13%. Energy drives most of the headline (+135.7% earnings growth). Ex-energy growth is about 17%. Analysts expect Q4 growth of +30.5%. JPMorgan has 2027 EPS growth slowing to +9.5%.

The BOJ held at 1.25% on an 8-1 vote (Takata dissented for a 25 bp hike). It surprised markets by raising its ETF sale pace to about 0.1% of market trading value from 0.05% (annual JPY860B versus JPY330B on book value), starting January 2027. It said underlying inflation is consistent with the 2% target, raised its FY27 core inflation forecast to 2.6% from 2.4%, and flagged another hike as likely.

Asian equities fell on tech weakness: Nikkei -2.12%, Shanghai -1.44%, Hang Seng +1.46%. Taiwan's Taiex closed at two-month lows near a technical correction. Samsung Electronics missed on Q3 net profit (KRW75T vs KRW86.1T consensus) and disappointed on shareholder returns. It guided capex up almost 60% to KRW84.4T for next year against a KRW74.4T consensus. Shares fell about 6%.

South Korea September industrial production rose 9.0% m/m, the strongest since February 2009, led by a 19.2% rise in semis (DRAM). Japan September industrial production rose 2.2% m/m against a 1.2% consensus, while retail sales fell 0.7% m/m against an expected +0.3%. Tokyo October core CPI was 2.6% y/y, in line.

market_movers.rationale: BofA cut to neutral from buy, citing lack of traction with external foundry customers and a sharp PC shipment decline.
Canaccord Genuity cut to hold from buy, citing softer legacy markets with no timeline on recovery, after a Q3 EPS miss and a guidance cut.
Citi upgraded Snam to hold, viewing lower 2027 regulated returns as temporary and largely reversing in 2028. It raised EPS estimates by about 4% from 2028.
Deutsche Bank upgraded Haleon to hold, citing weak H2 growth from structural channel shifts and poor execution, and argued the company needs a strategic reset.
Vontobel downgraded Sandoz to hold after a Q3 sales miss from German market conditions, biosimilar supply constraints and B2B headwinds.
DNB downgraded Boliden to hold. It said much of the 17% Q3 EBIT beat reflected lower-quality items, and weaker Aitik grades and higher smelter D&A cut 2028 estimates.
Berenberg downgraded Wacker Chemie to hold on limited 2027 EBITDA growth and uncertain benefits from the US Section 232 solar investigation.
Deutsche Bank downgraded Wacker Chemie to sell. Its 2027-29 estimates sit about 7% below consensus on medium-term earnings sustainability.
Deutsche Bank upgraded Aixtron to buy. Q3 orders more than doubled y/y to EUR275M on optoelectronics demand and an earlier power recovery. Execution and capacity ramp-up are the key constraints.
Citi upgraded COSCO SHIPPING Ports after Q3 results.

sector_views.rationale: AI capex and funding worries hit semis, memory, neoclouds, software and tech hardware. Equity digestion headwinds are building ahead of the Anthropic IPO.
Energy outperformed in the US as oil rose. It drives most of STOXX 600 Q3 earnings growth (+135.7%).
They outperformed in the US on Friday. In Europe, food & beverage, health care and household goods outperformed, driven by earnings.

earnings_insights: AMZN Q3, reported: AWS growth 39%, capex $77B (about $20B above consensus), TTM FCF -$42B, AWS backlog $578B. Q4 operating income guidance was below consensus at the midpoint. Retail and advertising missed consensus. Shares -1.4% in the Notable Movers list.

INTC Q3, reported: EPS beat, revenue missed. Client Computing revenue $8.1B (-5.1% y/y) against $8.95B consensus. Q4 EPS and revenue guidance below the Street. 2027 PC market expected -10%. Shares -28.6%.

RDDT Q3, reported: revenue, EPS and EBITDA beat, but DAUq missed on Google search referral headwinds. Q4 revenue and EBITDA guidance below consensus, with management warning DAUs could fall low-double-digits. ARPU was ahead of expectations. Shares -29.2%.

REGN Q3, reported: big beat on revenue and earnings, with strong US Eylea net sales growth, higher Sanofi collaboration revenue and Libtayo ahead of consensus. Full-year gross margin guidance raised. Shares +13.3%.

COIN Q3, reported: adjusted EBITDA beat on stronger subscription and services revenue (USDC, staking). Market share rose for a fourth straight quarter. Prediction markets passed a $200M annualized revenue run rate, while spot volumes and transaction revenue stayed pressured. Shares -10.6%.

SNDK F1Q, reported: EPS and revenue beat, F2Q guidance above consensus on data-center demand and NAND pricing. An 8-for-1 stock split was announced. There is debate on whether NAND pricing is near a cyclical peak. Shares -13.5%.

TWLO Q3, reported: revenue, EPS and operating income beat with 16% organic growth. FY26 guidance was raised, but preliminary FY27 organic growth of at least 10% was below bullish expectations. Shares -15.2%.
RBLX Q3, reported: bookings and DAUs beat. Q4 bookings and EBITDA guidance below consensus as AI infrastructure and marketing spend rises. Shares -18.1%.
ILMN Q3, reported: EPS beat, revenue light. FY26 EPS and revenue guidance raised. The stock was up 121% YTD before the print. Shares -18.6%.
PINS Q3, reported: revenue and EBITDA missed, MAUs a record 661M (+10% y/y). Q4 guidance below consensus on European cross-border advertiser weakness. Shares -2.8%.
SYK Q3, reported: EPS missed and revenue was light in both MedSurg/Neurotechnology and Orthopaedics. FY26 EPS and organic growth guidance cut. Shares -6.4%.
ATEC Q3, reported: revenue missed on lower biologics attachment and a 5% drop in revenue per case despite about 20% procedure volume growth. FY26 revenue, EBITDA and FCF guidance cut. Shares -38.1%.

Other US Q3 prints, reported: CPRI beat with FY27 outlook ahead (+16.3%). FDXF EPS $2.15 and revenue $3.30B for the four months to 30-Sep, guidance raised (+14.9%). RKT EPS beat, Q4 revenue guide missed (+7.4%). CBOE beat, FY26 organic net revenue growth guidance raised (+6.8%). RIVN beat, FY adjusted EBITDA and deliveries guidance midpoints raised (+6.2%). DXCM beat, FY revenue guide raised, new buyback up to $1B (+2.9%). CL beat, EPS growth outlook raised to 5-7% (+2.3%). CVX EPS and revenue beat, production below estimates (+1.8%). FSLR EPS beat, revenue missed, FY26 guidance cut (-1.4%).

European Q3 prints, reported: AZN revenue $16.2B (+7% CER, 2% above consensus) and core EPS $2.79 (9% ahead). SAN business operating income EUR5.43B against EUR4.32B consensus. BP net income $8.5B, underlying cash flow $14.3B. NWG adjusted PBT missed by 1%. CABK net profit beat by 8%. ETL-FR Q1 revenue EUR278.3M, 4.4% below company-compiled consensus.

Samsung Electronics Q3, reported: operating profit KRW107T (in line with preliminary), revenue KRW195T (in line), net profit KRW75T against KRW86.1T consensus. Semiconductor profit KRW106.5T against KRW108.5T consensus.

crypto_views: Binance confirmed $6.3B of funds impacted in a suspected hack, the biggest crypto heist on record. Binance froze $3B and temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals.
TRM Labs attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor. Tether and Circle froze $2.54B of linked assets.
Bitcoin futures fell 5.2%. Commentary flagged near-term risk to investor confidence and possible liquidity implications.
Coinbase said it was unaffected. Its Q3 adjusted EBITDA beat on USDC and staking revenue, prediction markets passed a $200M annualized revenue run rate, and the stock fell 10.6%.

Memory shortages and high component costs weigh on PC demand (INTC sees the PC market -10% in 2027).
Escalation in US-Iran tensions after the midterms, with oil already above $104.
Crypto exchange and liquidity risk after the Binance hack.
Further central bank tightening (Fed, ECB, BoE, BOJ) and energy-driven inflation.
Potential cyclical peak in NAND pricing (SNDK).
BOJ ETF sales could compound pessimism in a market downturn (MUFG Trust Bank).

Equal-weight RSP outpaced the cap-weighted S&P 500 by about 100 bp, with breadth only slightly negative.
Fresh equity supply is building: Alphabet's $85B, Intel's $23B and Meta's $25B offerings are underwater, with Anthropic's IPO expected in November.
geopolitical: US-Iran tensions: Iran insists on preconditions (ending the blockade, unfreezing assets, restarting oil sales) before nuclear talks resume. Renewed US strikes are possible after next Tuesday's midterm elections.
VP Vance's outreach to Iranian security chief Rezaei had little effect. Qatari negotiators are in Tehran, with talks that Reuters said are coordinated with the US.
US Section 232 announcements and investigations were cited as an uncertainty for First Solar and Wacker Chemie.
UK Chancellor Healey plans defense spending of 3% of GDP by 2030 and is discussing off-balance-sheet financing with at least three NATO members.
Chinese tourism to Japan more than halved after the diplomatic spat over PM Takaichi's remarks on Taiwan.
North Korea's TraderTraitor unit is blamed for the Binance hack.

tension_points.bull_case: AWS growth is projected at 40%+ in 2027 and 2028 with a path to $1T in AWS revenue, and backlog rose to $578B. Retail and ad softness was attributed to Prime Day timing.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex of $77B ran about $20B above consensus, TTM FCF is -$42B, and spending will rise 'meaningfully more' in 2027. Alphabet and Intel sit below their equity offering prices ahead of the Anthropic IPO.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further decline in recent megacap equity offerings below their issue prices, or a weak reception for Anthropic's expected November IPO.

tension_points.bull_case: Data Center/AI upside drove the Q3 EPS beat.
tension_points.bear_case: Client Computing revenue fell 5.1% to $8.1B and the PC market is expected to fall 10% in 2027. Negative FCF is expected, and BofA cited lack of traction with external foundry customers.

tension_points.bull_case: Lagarde said a hike was discussed, and Italy and France inflation accelerated, which supports a December hike.
tension_points.bear_case: A significant slowdown in activity into year-end would stop the hike. German inflation fell to 2.8%, and ECB staff estimate higher yields cut 2027-28 growth by 100 bps.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A significant slowdown in activity into year-end, or a notable drop in energy prices.
